v.why: Prior NAS-Bench-201 results show stacked 3x3 convs along 0->1->2 compose into a larger receptive field, so a conv on edge 0 is worth more when edge 2 is also a conv.
Prior benchmark results show that adding a direct input-to-output residual path to a cell lacking one helps much more than swapping skip in for an existing op.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 carries no signal, so a conv on edge 4 has almost nothing to act on.
With node 1 disconnected from the input, a conv on edge 2 is dead weight, so its benefit vanishes.
Pooling is known to be a weak learner in this space, so replacing a conv with it costs far more than replacing a weaker op.
Adding even a cheap 1x1 conv to an empty edge gives a large accuracy gain compared with swapping between existing ops.
Gains from extra 3x3 convs into the output saturate, so the edit helps less when the other output-side path is already a strong conv.
Filling an empty edge into the output node with a learnable op gives much more than the typical change between non-empty ops.
With edge 4 absent, edge 2 is the only route from node 1 to the output, so cutting it also makes edge 0 useless and hurts accuracy more.
A skip on the final edge gives a residual shortcut around a conv-heavy path on edge 2, which should ease optimization, so it should do better there than when edge 2 is weak.
